- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.17) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.28), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by +3–5% to align with true price momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30d forecast; apply a +2–4% upward bias to early days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.17 to -0.67), model fails to adjust; force a 3–5 day mean-reversion correction downward by 2–4% per day.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3 consecutive days, apply a “trend decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day for next 5 days.
